summary: Stateful TCP sequence rewriting by egress firewall causes gRPC frame reordering and corrupted model stream in Private VPC
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a Private deployment report intermittent corruption of streaming model responses (missing tokens, truncated arrays) when using long-lived gRPC streams. The symptoms began after a change to the customer's stateful egress firewall appliance last week.

Impact:
- FinSight Analytics reports production inference errors for chat sessions (several sessions per hour).
- Affects models served from the customer's private cluster (gRPC streaming generation).
- User-visible: dropped or out-of-order token sequences and occasional model shard fetch retries leading to latency spikes.

Environment:
- Private deployment in customer VPC (us-east).
- Egress path: customer stateful NGFW -> transit VPC -> Redwood VPCE.
- Traffic: long-lived HTTP/2/gRPC connections carrying multiplexed frames and range downloads for large model shards.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create long-lived streaming chat session against private endpoint (gRPC bidi).
2) Generate responses using >= 2k token context and enable content-range shard downloads.
3) Observe session for 10+ minutes under moderate concurrency (10-20 circuits).
4) Intermittently see token order anomalies or truncated frames; shard reassembly errors appear in serving logs.

Expected behaviour:
- gRPC frames arrive and are reassembled in-order; model token stream is continuous and error-free.

Actual behaviour:
- Frames appear reordered at application layer causing JSON/stream parsing failures, partial arrays, and shard integrity mismatches. TCP layer shows no obvious retransmit bursts.
steps_to_reproduce: (short) Start private gRPC stream with large context tokens and concurrent shard downloads; run for 10+ minutes; packet-capture through egress appliance shows sequence number adjustments interleaved with normal traffic.
logs:
serving-node.log excerpt:
[2026-03-12T09:21:13Z] WARN stream: reassembly mismatch: expected seq 13842 got 13848
[2026-03-12T09:21:13Z] ERROR grpc: recv frame out-of-order, dropping frame id=0x7f3a
[2026-03-12T09:21:13Z] ERROR shard-fetch: checksum mismatch for shard-4 (range offset 1048576)

tcpdump capture (from customer egress interface):
15:21:13.123456 IP a.b.c.d.443 > e.f.g.h.32768: Flags [.], seq 13840:13848, ack 24012 win 65535
15:21:13.123457 IP a.b.c.d.443 > e.f.g.h.32768: Flags [.], seq 13848:13856, ack 24012
-- customer appliance rewrites show non-monotonic seq adjustments for overlapping segments
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-12 10:00 UTC: Customer opened with evidence of token order corruption and shard integrity errors.
- 2026-03-12 12:00 UTC: SRE requested pcap across egress appliance and serving node for correlation.
- 2026-03-12 14:30 UTC: Packet captures show TCP sequence number normalization and segment coalescing by customer's NGFW.
- 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC: Replayed capture in lab: when NGFW configured with sequence-normalization and TCP-segment-merge enabled, gRPC multiplexed frames suffered application-level reordering despite TCP ACKs remaining normal.

Hypotheses tested:
- Hypothesis A: MTU/PMTU fragmentation — ruled out: no ICMP fragmentation seen and packet sizes consistent.
- Hypothesis B: Transparent proxy altering ALPN/headers — partial: ALPN preserved.
- Hypothesis C: Stateful sequence-number normalization or segment re-segmentation by middlebox — reproduced in lab and correlates with serving errors.

Correlated references: #support Slack thread, lab-replay PR https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/5421, see runbook page above.
root_cause: A customer-managed stateful NGFW was applying TCP sequence-number normalization and aggressive segment coalescing for perceived reassembly optimization. This middlebox behavior rewrites segment boundaries in a way that breaks HTTP/2/gRPC multiplexing assumptions at the application layer, producing out-of-order frames and shard reassembly checksum failures without triggering TCP-level retransmits.
resolution:
Workaround applied:
- Customer disabled 'TCP sequence normalization' and 'segment coalescing' features on the egress NGFW appliance for traffic to the Redwood VPCE.
- Immediately after the change, SRE observed no further frame reordering in packet captures and serving logs returned to normal.
Fix plan:
- Short-term: Rolling patch to serving runtime to add detection and early-drop for corrupted multiplexed frames (PR queued).
- Long-term: Add a diagnostic check in the Private deployment onboarding checklist to detect middlebox TCP-normalization heuristics and document recommended NGFW settings.
resolution_notes: Customer applied the workaround at 2026-03-13T17:22Z; FinSight confirmed reduced errors and resumed normal traffic. Patch PR for detection: https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/5421. Follow-up runbook update scheduled.
follow_up: Add a Private deployment test to detect TCP sequence normalization during validation (SRE ticket).
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to update onboarding checklist and docs for NGFW settings.
Consider automated alerting when serving logs report repeated reassembly mismatches tied to a single customer egress IP.
